subject: Re: AsterBank MSA - questions on usage measurement: dispute window + audit rights
related_links: Jira: SUP-3160 (reference for streaming disconnect explanation pattern)
body:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 9:14 AM
Subject: Fwd: AsterBank MSA - questions on usage measurement: dispute window + audit rights

Sofia/Michael/Laura,

Forwarding questions from AsterBank’s counsel. They’re pushing for a longer dispute window and broader audit rights (incl. raw logs). Can you advise what’s acceptable + provide language we can send back?

Context: They’re doing a VPC/Private deployment with an enterprise procurement motion, but we’re still using usage-based line items for the pilot period.

Thanks,
Jordan

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference


---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Dana Pierce <dana.pierce@piercelegal.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 8:52 AM
Subject: AsterBank / Redwood Inference - Measurement & Billing (questions)
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Shah <maya.shah@asterbank.com>

Jordan,

We reviewed the “Measurement and Billing” language. A few questions/requests:

1) Dispute window: We cannot accept a 30-day window for disputes of usage-based charges. We typically require 12 months, or at least 180 days, given our internal invoice review cycles.

2) Audit rights: The current draft references an “audit” but is unclear on scope and access. We require (a) audit rights by our internal audit team or an independent auditor, (b) access to records sufficient to validate measurement (including source logs), and (c) a minimum 2-year lookback.

3) Failed requests/retries: Please confirm whether retries, timeouts, or partial streaming responses are billable.

Please propose revised language.

Best regards,
Dana Pierce
Pierce Legal LLP
Counsel to AsterBank



From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 10:07 AM
Subject: Re: Fwd: AsterBank MSA - questions on usage measurement: dispute window + audit rights

Thanks Jordan.

Initial POV (happy to adjust based on your views):

- Dispute window: we can move off 30 days for an enterprise/bank, but 12 months is too open-ended. Suggest 90 days from invoice date for usage disputes, with a requirement to pay undisputed amounts.

- Audit: we should allow an audit of our “usage measurement and billing records” (reports/aggregates + supporting documentation), but NOT raw event logs or anything that creates security risk / exposes other customers or platform internals. Provide (i) invoice line item mapping, (ii) customer-specific usage export (meter + dimensions), and (iii) reconciliation summary for the invoice run.

- Lookback: 12 months is reasonable; 2 years is probably unnecessary.

- Retries/failed requests/streams: we should stick to our product definition: bill for successful tokens returned to client; do not bill tokens generated after client disconnect; failed requests may still have input tokens depending on where failure occurs (but we can define “billable usage” in terms of request_outcome).

Michael: can you confirm acceptable audit language / any hard lines?
Laura: any Finance constraints on dispute window / billing correction timelines?

I can draft a response email + proposed redline language today.

Sofia

—
Sofia Ivanova
Commercial Counsel, Redwood Inference


From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 10:31 AM
Subject: Re: Fwd: AsterBank MSA - questions on usage measurement: dispute window + audit rights

Agree with your direction.

Hard lines:
- No raw logs. We can provide customer-specific usage reports and reasonable supporting documentation, but not system-level telemetry or anything that could compromise security / reveal other customers’ data.
- Audit: limited to verifying fees billed under the Agreement, once per 12-month period, during normal business hours, with reasonable advance notice, and subject to confidentiality.
- Lookback: 12 months max.

Dispute window: 90 days is ok. We should require disputes be submitted with reasonable detail (invoice number, endpoints/models/time window, claimed delta) and that they raise it promptly once discovered.

On retries/failed requests: we should avoid promising that “failed requests are never billable.” Instead define “Billable Usage” as measured per our documentation and reflected in the usage reports. We can explicitly exclude tokens generated after disconnect; that’s safe.

If they insist on 180 days, we can consider 120; 12 months is not acceptable.

Michael

—
Michael Grant
General Counsel, Redwood Inference


From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 11:02 AM
Subject: Re: Fwd: AsterBank MSA - questions on usage measurement: dispute window + audit rights

Finance constraints:

- We can operationalize 90 days without causing close/audit headaches, as long as we keep “pay undisputed amounts” and require specifics in the dispute notice.
- We do not want open-ended clawbacks against quarters already closed. 12 months would require special handling and increases audit exposure.

On audit: +1 to no raw logs. We can provide invoice support packs (customer usage export + mapping + reconciliation summary) and, if needed, a joint working session to walk them through meter definitions.

Jordan: I’d position this as “auditability without exposing platform internals” + we already have strong internal controls around metering.

Laura

—
Laura Bennett
VP Finance (Exec Sponsor), Redwood Inference


From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Pierce <dana.pierce@piercelegal.com>
Cc: Maya Shah <maya.shah@asterbank.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 12:18 PM
Subject: Re: AsterBank / Redwood Inference - Measurement & Billing (questions)
Attachments: Redwood_Inference_Measurement_and_Billing_Language_v2026-02-06.docx, Metering_Definitions_Appendix_-_Hosted_API_v3_excerpt.pdf

Dana,

Thank you for the detailed questions. We can accommodate revisions that provide a clear, auditable process for validating usage-based charges, while also protecting security and other customers’ confidentiality.

Below are our proposed positions, and I’ve attached updated language for your review.

1) Dispute window
We can extend the dispute window to ninety (90) days from the invoice date for usage-based charges, provided AsterBank pays all undisputed amounts on time and includes reasonable detail in any dispute notice (invoice number, affected services/endpoints, time window, and the basis for the dispute).

2) Audit rights (scope)
We can provide audit rights limited to verification of fees billed under the Agreement based on our measurement and billing records. We can provide customer-specific usage reports/exports, invoice line item mapping, and supporting documentation sufficient to validate the measurement.

We cannot provide access to raw system telemetry logs or information that could compromise platform security or reveal other customers’ data.

We propose: one audit in any 12-month period, with reasonable advance notice, during normal business hours, conducted by AsterBank’s internal audit function or an independent auditor (subject to confidentiality).

Lookback: up to twelve (12) months.

3) Failed requests / retries / streaming
Billable usage is determined based on the billable usage reports generated from the services. Generally:
- We do not bill tokens generated after a client disconnects from a streaming response.
- Retries may result in additional billable usage when a customer retries a request (i.e., a new request is processed).
- We can walk your team through how outcomes are reflected in the usage export (e.g., request outcome categories).

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute working session next week with our finance/billing controls team to walk through an example invoice support pack.

Best,
Sofia

—
Sofia Ivanova
Commercial Counsel, Redwood Inference


From: Dana Pierce <dana.pierce@piercelegal.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Shah <maya.shah@asterbank.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 10:46 AM
Subject: Re: AsterBank / Redwood Inference - Measurement & Billing (questions)

Sofia,

Appreciate the revisions. A few follow-ups:

- Dispute window: 90 days is still difficult for us. Our internal policy is 180 days for usage/variable charges.

- Audit: We need the audit to include access to underlying records sufficient to validate the metering. If raw logs are not available, please specify exactly what is available (fields, granularity, retention). We also request a 24-month lookback.

- Streaming: Please confirm in the contract (not only “generally”) that tokens generated after client disconnect are not billable.

Thanks,
Dana


From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Pierce <dana.pierce@piercelegal.com>
Cc: Maya Shah <maya.shah@asterbank.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 4:38 PM
Subject: Re: AsterBank / Redwood Inference - Measurement & Billing (questions)

Dana,

Understood. We can propose the following compromise, which I believe addresses AsterBank’s process needs while remaining operationally and security-feasible on our side:

1) Dispute window
We can extend to one hundred twenty (120) days from invoice date for usage-based charges (with the same requirements: pay undisputed amounts; dispute notice includes reasonable detail). We’re not able to go to 180 days.

2) Audit scope + underlying records
We will specify in the clause that the “underlying records” available for audit consist of customer-specific, itemized usage exports at request-level granularity (where applicable) including service/endpoint, model identifier, region, timestamps (UTC), and the applicable meter quantities reflected on the invoice.

We will also provide:
- the invoice line-item-to-meter mapping used for the invoice run;
- applicable meter definitions/rounding rules in effect for the billed period;
- reconciliation summaries for the invoice run.

We cannot provide raw platform telemetry logs beyond those customer-specific exports.

Lookback: we can agree to twelve (12) months. We’re not able to support a 24-month lookback.

3) Streaming disconnects
We can add an explicit statement in the measurement language that tokens generated after a client disconnects from a streaming response are not billable.

If you’d like, we can set up a working session early next week with our finance and billing controls lead to show the exact usage export format and a sample “invoice support pack.” That often resolves the concern about “what records exist” much faster than iterating on hypotheticals.

Best,
Sofia

—
Sofia Ivanova
Commercial Counsel, Redwood Inference
